column1: # splunk-precedence-allowlist.tsv — Splunk searches that mix OR and NOT in one paren
# scope, each reviewed once and signed off.
# WHY. pySigma's Splunk backend does not parenthesise a top-level OR against a top-level
# NOT, so `(a) OR (b) NOT (filter)` is correct only under the search command's documented
# precedence (parentheses, NOT, OR, AND). It is right today; it is one reading away from
# letting a branch escape its filter, and eval/where evaluate AND before OR. See #166.
# check-splunk-precedence.sh flags every such search and fails unless it has a row here,
# so the next one is a review conversation rather than a silent behaviour change. A row
# is NOT a suppression — it is a record that someone traced the binding and found it
# sound. The reason column is required and may not be '-'.
# Keyed on stanza title because the generated conf carries no rule path. Retitling a rule
# drops it out of this list and fails the gate, which is the right direction to be wrong.

column2: Collected data staged into an archive (T1560.001)
column3: sigma condition is `selection_password or (1 of selection_staging_* and not filter_backup_tooling)`; the backend groups the outer OR but leaves `(staging) OR (compress-archive) NOT ParentImage=backup-agent` ungrouped inside it. Under search precedence that is (staging OR compress) AND NOT backup-agent, which is the intent: the password branch is deliberately unfiltered, the two staging-path branches are both filtered. Predates #166 and is unchanged by it

column2: Mass file read - local data collection sweep (T1005)
column3: sigma condition is `(selection_list or selection_mask) and not filter_indexers`; the backend emits `source= (list) OR (mask) NOT (indexers)`. Under search precedence the leading source= term AND the filter both bind to both branches, which is the intent. Long-form note lives in the rule's own description (#165)

column2: Data encrypted for impact - BitLocker driven from the command line
column3: sigma condition is `1 of selection_* and not filter_provisioning`; the backend emits `(manage-bde) OR (powershell cmdlet) NOT ParentImage=*\\TSManager.exe`. Under search-command precedence (parens, NOT, OR, AND) the NOT binds to its own term first and the juxtaposed implicit AND binds loosest, so it reads ((manage-bde) OR (cmdlet)) AND NOT TSManager - the imaging filter covers BOTH branches, which is the intent: a task sequence drives manage-bde and Enable-BitLocker alike, so neither branch should alert on it. Same shape and same reading as the archive-staging row above. Added with the filter in #261

column2: AWS snapshot/AMI shared outside the organisation (T1537)
column3: sigma condition is `selection_grant and (selection_public or (selection_named and not filter_own_accounts))`; the backend emits `eventSource= eventName= (public x3) OR (named x3 NOT (own-accounts x3))`. Under search-command precedence (parens, NOT, OR, AND) the inner paren reads (named1 OR named2 OR named3) AND NOT (own-accounts), so the allowlist covers all three named branches; the outer OR group then binds under the two juxtaposed IN terms, so eventSource and eventName gate every branch. The three public branches sitting OUTSIDE that paren is the INTENT, not a miss - a `group: all` share is public and no account allowlist can make it benign, which is the whole two-tier design (#262). Same shape and reading as the archive-staging and BitLocker rows above

sigma condition is `1 of selection_* and not filter_iac`; the backend emits `(setMetadata + added_metadata_keys) OR (setMetadata + modified_metadata_keys) NOT principal_email=iac`. Under search-command precedence (parens, NOT, OR, AND) the NOT binds to its own term first and the juxtaposed implicit AND binds loosest, so it reads ((added) OR (modified)) AND NOT iac - the IaC allowlist covers BOTH arms, which is the intent: a provisioning principal writing a startup script is benign whether the key is new on the instance or overwrites an existing one, so exempting only one arm would leave the other alerting on every image build. Same shape and same reading as the BitLocker and archive-staging rows above. Added with the rule in #305

column2: Mass service stop - the ransomware pre-encryption teardown (T1489)
column3: sigma condition (base rule service_stop_command) is `1 of selection_* and not filter_maintenance_parent`; the backend emits `(net stop) OR (sc stop/disable) OR (taskkill /f) OR (Stop-Service/Stop-Process) NOT ParentImage=maintenance` as the leading search command, ahead of `| bin | stats dc(CommandLine)`. Under search-command precedence (parens, NOT, OR, AND) the NOT binds to its own term first and the juxtaposed implicit AND binds loosest, so it reads (net OR sc OR taskkill OR powershell) AND NOT maintenance - the allowlist covers all four arms before the count, which is the intent: a suite's restart tooling mixes net, sc and PowerShell stops, and exempting only one arm would leave the others counting toward the burst. Same shape and same reading as the BitLocker row above. Added with the filter in #324
